He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond Spiders]]. Gilyard is the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career steals leaders|all-time NCAA career steals leader]], breaking the previous record of 385 on December 5, 2021, and finishing his career with 466 steals. ==High school career== Gilyard played basketball for [[The Barstow School]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]] under the coaching of former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Billy Thomas (basketball)|Billy Thomas]]. As a sophomore, he helped win the Missouri Class 3 state championship, his program's first state title since 1995, after scoring 16 points in a 61–46 win over Strafford High School.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=McDowell|title=Barstow beats Strafford 61-46, wins Missouri Class 3 boys basketball state championship|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/missouri-prep-basketball/article14458142.html|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=March 14, 2015|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On December 5, 2016, during his senior season, Gilyard scored a school-record 50 points in an 85–47 victory over [[Washington High School (Missouri)|Washington High School]].{{cite web|first=Sam|last=McDowell|title=Barstow senior Jacob Gilyard breaks school record with 50 points in a game|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/missouri-prep-basketball/article119100393.html|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=December 6, 2016|access-date=March 15, 2020}} He finished the season averaging 33.2 points and seven assists per game, was named Class 3 Player of the Year and won the DiRenna Award as the top player in the Kansas City area.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=McDowell|title=Barstow's Jacob Gilyard, St. Pius X's Abby Hipp win DiRenna Awards as KC's top hoopsters|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/article143246574.html|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=April 6, 2017|access-date=March 15, 2020}} A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Gilyard committed to play collegiately for [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]] on September 12, 2016.{{cite web|first=Grant|last=Kelly|title=2017 point guard Jacob Gilyard commits to Richmond|url=https://www.a10talk.com/2017-point-guard-jacob-gilyard-commits-richmond/|website=A10Talk.com|publisher=A10 Talk|date=September 13, 2016|access-date=March 15, 2020}} He did not receive any offers from [[Power Five conferences|Power Five]] programs.{{cite web|first=John|last=O'Connor|title=At 5-foot-9, 160 pounds, UR's Jacob Gilyard has the ball, the green light, and the ability to dominate|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-richmond/at--foot--pounds-ur-s-jacob-gilyard-has/article_c543df7a-45f2-55c3-80be-ee23b3ef4930.html|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=January 27, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} ==College career== [[File:Jacob Gilyard.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Gilyard in March 2019]] On December 10, 2017, Gilyard scored a freshman season-high 23 points with five three-pointers in a 74–71 win over [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]]. He made the game-winning three-pointer with 0.4 seconds left.{{cite web|first=John|last=O'Connor|title=Jacob Gilyard's 3 shoots Richmond by JMU in final second|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/jacob-gilyard-s-shoots-richmond-by-jmu-in-final-second/article_4ca241e5-8c3f-5939-8634-948df2d8d961.html|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=December 10, 2017|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On February 28, 2018, Gilyard recorded 13 points, six assists and three steals in a 90–65 win over [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]], surpassing [[Kenny Atkinson]]'s school freshman assist record and becoming the first [[NCAA Division I]] freshman to reach 80 steals since [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]]'s [[Marcus Smart]] in 2013.{{cite web|title=Golden's 26 leads Richmond over UMass 90-65|url=http://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/ncb/id/22609095|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 28, 2018|access-date=March 15, 2020}} He closed the season with 89 steals, breaking the program record previously held by [[Tony Dobbins]]. As a freshman, Gilyard averaged 11.4 points, 4.1 assists and 2.8 steals per game, which ranked sixth in the country, and started in all 32 games.{{cite web|first=John|last=O'Connor|title=Freshman Jacob Gilyard stealing his way to Chief Thief status at UR|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-richmond/freshman-jacob-gilyard-stealing-his-way-to-chief-thief-status/article_6a2ff075-7430-5130-9dce-bbd260b3feb8.html|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=March 15, 2020}} In the third game of his sophomore season, on November 16, 2018, Gilyard scored a season-high 31 points, 27 of which came in the second half, and recorded six assists in a 78–70 victory over [[IUPUI Jaguars men's basketball|IUPUI]].{{cite web|first=John|last=O'Connor|title=Jacob Gilyard (31 points) gives UR turbo-spark in second half of 78-70 win over IUPUI|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-richmond/jacob-gilyard-points-gives-ur-turbo-spark-in-second-half/article_b210ff80-7fd2-5b8f-a56d-a2e47347cdb1.html|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On February 11, 2019, he was named [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] Player of the Week for his first time after averaging 22.5 points, 5.5 assists and five steals per game in wins over [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] and [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]].{{cite web|title=Jacob Gilyard Named A-10 Player of the Week|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2019/2/11/mens-basketball-jacob-gilyard-named-a-10-player-of-the-week.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=February 11, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} Gilyard averaged 16.2 points, 5.2 assists and 2.8 steals per game as a sophomore, earning second-team All-Atlantic 10 and Atlantic 10 All-Defensive Team honors.{{cite web|title=Gilyard, Golden Earn All-Conference Honors From A-10|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2019/3/12/mens-basketball-gilyard-golden-earn-all-conference-honors-from-a-10.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} He joined [[Allen Iverson]] and [[Jason Kidd]] as the only Division I players since 1992 to record at least 868 points, 290 assists and 177 steals by the end of their sophomore seasons.{{cite web|title=Jacob Gilyard|url=https://richmondspiders.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jacob-gilyard/3572|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On November 18, 2019, Gilyard was recognized as Atlantic 10 Co-Player of the Week after averaging 22.0 points, 5.5 assists and four steals per game in victories over [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] and [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]].{{cite web|title=Gilyard Named A-10 Co-Player of the Week|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2019/11/18/gilyard-named-a-10-co-player-of-the-week.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=November 18, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On December 9, he was again named conference Co-Player of the Week after averaging 16.5 points, 8.5 assists, six rebounds and five steals in wins over [[Hampton Pirates men's basketball|Hampton]] and [[South Alabama Jaguars men's basketball|South Alabama]].{{cite web|title=Gilyard Nabs Second A-10 Player of the Week Honor of Season|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2019/12/9/mens-basketball-gilyard-nabs-second-a-10-player-of-the-week-honor-of-season.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=December 9, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} Against Hampton, Gilyard registered his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]], with 18 points and a season-high 10 assists, and scored his 1,000th career point.{{cite web|title=Backcourt Leads Short-Handed Spiders Over Hampton|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2019/12/3/mens-basketball-backcourt-leads-short-handed-spiders-over-hampton.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=December 3, 2019|access-date=March 15, 2020}} On January 25, 2020, he scored a season-high 29 points in an 87–79 loss to seventh-ranked [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]].{{cite web|title=Gilyard's 29 Not Enough For Spiders In Loss To #7 Dayton|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2020/1/25/mens-basketball-gilyards-29-not-enough-for-spiders-in-loss-to-7-dayton.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=January 25, 2020|access-date=March 15, 2020}} As a junior, Gilyard was named Atlantic 10 Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-Atlantic 10 after averaging 12.7 points, 5.7 assists, a Division I-high 3.2 steals and 3.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Gilyard Wins A-10 Defensive Player of the Year As Three Spiders Earn All-Conference Honors|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2020/3/10/mens-basketball-gilyard-wins-a-10-defensive-player-of-the-year-as-three-spiders-earn-all-conference-honors.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|publisher=University of Richmond Athletics|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 15, 2020}} Following the season Gilyard declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Francis, Gilyard, Golden to Enter 2020 NBA Draft, Maintain Eligibility|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2020/4/6/mens-basketball-francis-gilyard-golden-to-enter-2020-nba-draft-maintain-eligibility.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|date=April 6, 2020|access-date=April 11, 2020}} On May 21, Gilyard announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning for his senior season at Richmond.{{cite news|first=Ethan|last=Cadeaux|title=Report: Richmond guard Jacob Gilyard plans to withdraw from NBA Draft and return to school|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/ncaa/report-richmond-guard-jacob-gilyard-plans-withdraw-nba-draft-and-return-school|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=May 21, 2020|access-date=August 2, 2020}} Gilyard took advantage of the NCAA offer of an extra year of eligibility due to the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on college athletics, choosing to return for a fifth year.{{cite web|title=Jacob Gilyard Announces He Will Return to Richmond Next Season|url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2021/3/28/mens-basketball-jacob-gilyard-announces-he-will-return-to-richmond-next-season.aspx|website=RichmondSpiders.com|date=March 28, 2020|access-date=April 2, 2021}} He was named to the Third Team All-Atlantic 10 as well as the All-Defensive Team.{{cite press release|title=Brajkovic Named Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, McKillop, Osunniyi Earn Top Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies / Hustle (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Gilyard signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on September 23, 2022,{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies announce 2022 training camp roster|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-announce-2022-training-camp-roster-220923|website=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2022|access-date=October 9, 2022}} but was waived on October 10.{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|title=The @memgrizz today announced the team signed Matthew Hurt and Sean McDermott. In addition, the Grizzlies waived Justin Bean and Jacob Gilyard.|number=1579471960823992320|user=GrizzliesPR|date=October 10, 2022|access-date=February 23, 2024}} On October 23, he joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2022-23 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=February 24, 2024}} On April 8, 2023, Gilyard signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Grizzlies{{cite tweet|user=GrizzliesPR|title=The @memgrizz today announced the team signed Kenneth Lofton Jr. to a multi-year contract. In related moves, the Grizzlies signed Jacob Gilyard to a two-way contract and waived Kennedy Chandler.|number=1644772706255097863|author=Grizzlies PR|date=April 8, 2023|access-date=April 8, 2023}} becoming one of only two active NBA players below 6" tall.{{cite web|first=Max|last=Goodwin|title=From KC to Memphis Grizzlies, Jacob Gilyard shining in NBA|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/article282232298.html|work=KC Star|date=November 23, 2023|access-date=November 23, 2023}} The next day, he made his NBA debut in a 115–100 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he recorded three points, seven assists, four rebounds, and three steals. After 20 games, he led the Grizzlies in three-point shooting percentage at 42.9%.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies 2023-24 NBA Regular Season Stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/team/stats/_/name/mem/sort/threePointPct|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 19, 2023}} On February 24, 2024, he was waived by Memphis.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Jordan Goodwin to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jordan-goodwin-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2024|access-date=February 24, 2024}}
